options: The distribution of data values within a single sample.
The distribution of all possible sample statistics (e.g., means) from repeated random samples of the same size from a population.
The distribution of the population statistics (e.g., means) based on the sample statistic we observed.
The distribution of errors that occur when sampling.

Q6. A researcher collects a random sample of 80 students from a university (40 students are freshmen and 40 students are seniors). 

The researcher investigated whether freshmen and seniors differ in their anxiety scores.
lm(anxiety_score~college_year, data = collegedata)

The estimated b₁ from the sample is 1.2, indicating that, on average, seniors score 1.2 points higher in anxiety than freshmen.

The 95% confidence interval for β₁ is [0.2, 2.2]. 

a) Based on this confidence interval, do you think freshmen and seniors differ in their average anxiety levels (i.e., would you reject the empty model)? Explain your reasoning.
b) Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the confidence interval [0.2, 2.2]?
options: There is a 95% chance the true mean difference between freshmen and seniors lies between 0.2 and 2.2.
95% of students have an anxiety score between 0.2 and 2.2.
If we repeated this study many times, 95% of such intervals would contain the true mean difference between freshmen and seniors.
The population mean difference is guaranteed to be between 0.2 and 2.2.

Suppose we want to estimate a population parameter, such as the average happiness level in a country. A common approach is to draw a sample and compute the mean of the sample, which serves as our point estimate of the population mean. However, because we usually have access to only one sample, this single estimate does not capture the uncertainty inherent in sampling. To address this, we construct a confidence interval (CI)—a range of plausible values for the population parameter of interest, derived from our observed sample data.

Next, you will watch 3 instructional videos about the confidence interval. Feel free to fullscreen for better viewing. Do not skip any part of the video, move back or rewatch. The option to advance the page will appear after each video ends.
